questions.q: Why is Microsoft Purview described as a "cross-platform metadata hub"?
options: Because its Data Map is explicitly built to reach into other vendors' platforms (Microsoft 365, Azure, AWS, even Snowflake), governing assets it doesn't itself store or compute
Because Purview can only govern data stored inside Purview itself
Because Purview replaces the need for any other platform's governance features
Because Purview is exclusively a security product, not a governance one
questions.explain: Purview's own course describes its Data Map connecting to sources across many vendors, which is exactly what makes its reach cross-platform rather than single-platform.

questions.q: Why does a permission mistake in Microsoft Fabric tend to be tenant-wide by default?
options: Because every Fabric workload — lakehouse, warehouse, BI, pipelines — stores its data in one shared tenant-wide lake, OneLake
Because Fabric has no access control features at all
Because Fabric only supports a single user per tenant
Because Fabric workloads each use entirely separate, disconnected storage
questions.explain: Fabric's own governance course is explicit that the shared OneLake architecture — not separate storage per workload — is why mistakes have tenant-wide reach by default.

questions.q: What problem did Databricks Unity Catalog solve that existed before it, according to the lesson?
options: Permissions, auditing, and lineage were set per workspace, with no single answer to "who can see this table, anywhere"
Databricks previously had no way to run SQL queries at all
Databricks tables could not be organized into schemas before Unity Catalog existed
Unity Catalog was built to replace Databricks' compute engine
questions.explain: Unity Catalog centralizes governance into one metastore across workspaces (even across clouds) instead of per-workspace permissions.

questions.q: Ordering the four platforms from narrowest to widest governance reach, which order does the lesson give?
options: Snowflake, then Databricks Unity Catalog, then Microsoft Fabric, then Microsoft Purview
Microsoft Purview, then Snowflake, then Microsoft Fabric, then Databricks Unity Catalog
All four platforms have exactly the same governance reach
Microsoft Fabric, then Snowflake, then Microsoft Purview, then Databricks Unity Catalog
questions.explain: The lesson orders them by reach: Snowflake (its own engine), Unity Catalog (across Databricks workspaces/clouds), Fabric (across workload types within one product), Purview (across platforms entirely).

questions.q: According to the lesson, how do Microsoft Fabric's native governance and Microsoft Purview relate to each other?
options: Purview integration extends Fabric's native governance rather than replacing it, for organizations that need governance beyond Fabric alone
Purview and Fabric cannot be used together under any circumstances
Purview completely replaces every native Fabric governance feature once adopted
Fabric's governance course has no mention of Purview at all
questions.explain: Fabric's own governance course lists Purview integration as one of its chapters — the lesson uses this as the concrete example of platforms composing rather than competing.
